notes.about: Bengali's own rules. The engine's copy of the rules for a beng pack without this file is Assamese's (it folds র to ৰ), so the Bengali pack always carries this one.
notes.block: Bengali-Assamese, U+0980-U+09FF. Words are runs of these letters and signs.
notes.notWord: Digits ০-৯ and the currency and fraction signs are not word letters. Nor are ৰ (U+09F0) and ৱ (U+09F1): they are Assamese letters, so a token with one is Assamese text in a Bengali source and is not counted. Bengali's র (U+09B0) is kept as it is; nothing is folded.
notes.replace: After NFC: ত + virama + ZWJ is the old encoding of khanda ta ৎ. Two mis-encodings common in the dumps are mended: া + ে (the halves of ো in visual order) becomes ো, and অ + া becomes আ. NFC leaves য়, ড়, ঢ় as base + nukta (U+09BC), since U+09DC/09DD/09DF are composition exclusions. Every ZWJ and ZWNJ is dropped (no "joiners" field), as for Hindi and Assamese: র‍্য (র + ZWJ + virama + য, as in র‍্যাব) is stored and typed as র্য.
notes.apostrophe: Bengali does not write an apostrophe inside words the way Assamese does (হ'ল), so it ends a word.
notes.phraseBreaks: Bengali ends a sentence with the danda । (U+0964); ॥ ends verse. Next-word pairs never span one.
notes.signs: A vowel sign or virama must follow a base: a word with one after another vowel or sign is mis-encoded text and is not counted. ং ঁ ঃ may follow a vowel and are not in the list.
notes.bases: The consonants, the nukta, and two vowels: অ and এ take the -ya sign and আ-kar to write the vowel of English "and" (অ্যাপ, অ্যান্ড, এ্যান্ড), which is ordinary modern spelling. The text has such a word about 3 times in 1,000 (298,000 of 107 million).
